  "limitations_stated": [
    "The amount of available evidence and the overall quality are limited.",
    "There is high variability between study types.",
    "The observed range of translational success rates, and the lack of a clear relationship with any of the analysed factors, might indicate that translational success is unpredictable.",
    "The risk of bias of the included studies was high.",
    "Much of the included evidence is older.",
    "The cumulative evidence of current papers on this topic is insufficient.",
    "Scoping searches resulted in large numbers of retrieved references, with limited sensitivity.",
    "The search strategy missed papers only describing translation or predictivity in the abstract or the text body while not being indexed for them.",
    "Snowballing via reference lists is not an optimal method in this field due to suboptimal referencing practices and difficulty identifying relevant studies.",
    "A limitation is that a term for modelling and scaling studies was not included in the search.",
    "The search was performed halfway October 2017.",
    "Not all available evidence has been included.",
    "Dependency of the data: several authors and research groups publish multiple papers on translational success rates, often based on (partially) overlapping data sets.",
    "The use of different measures for translational success, based on different definitions, using different diagnostic statistics.",
    "The percentage overlap in CIs, used for meta-analyses, is disputable.",
    "Dosing and incidence of events are often disregarded.",
    "Publication bias (i.e. the relative underreporting of primary studies with negative and neutral results) can obscure translational failure rates.",
    "The observed range of translational success was not drastically affected by publication date or manner of publication retrieval.",
    "Data extraction and analysis were not performed in a blinded manner.",
    "The risk of bias of the included studies was high.",
    "Many reviews did not comply with the PRISMA guidelines.",
    "Many of the included reviews had drugs as the experimental unit, and most did not describe their selection of the drugs.",
    "Explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria were scarce.",
    "The data presented in this paper have severe limitations and should be considered inconclusive and used for hypothesis-generation only.",
    "Reliably determining actual translational success rates is unmanageable as long as the current status of reporting of preclinical research leaves room for improvement, and non-reproducibility is such a critical issue in both animal and human studies."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "81 out of the 121 references had a high risk of funding bias.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "The published translational success rates range from 0 to 100%.",

    "For studies using quantitative definitions of translation, translational success rates ranged from 0 to 100%.",
    "For the 8 studies analysing events, the translational success rate ranged from 7 to 74%.",
    "The studies with n > 200 are all toxicology studies using a binary definition of translation.",
    "The range of published translational success rates is 0% to 100%.",

    "Out of 287 registered drugs that were tested in rats and mice for carcinogenicity, results were concordant with humans for 146.",

    "70% of human adverse events was predicted by animal models.",

    "18 out of the 53 physical signs observed in man were predicted correctly in rats; 29 out of the 53 in dogs.",
    "Out of the 86 physical signs analysed in animals, 64 accurately reflected occurrence or absence in man.",

    "In any species tested, 71% of human adverse events was predicted.",
    "37% of adverse drug reactions in humans were predicted from animal studies.",

    "The authors presented the sensitivity (73%), positive predictive value (20%), negative predictive value (90%) and crude data.",

    "R 2 = 0.97; bioavailability correlates to some extent between monkeys and humans: R 2 = 0.50; clearance correlates between monkeys and humans: R 2 = 0.82; time to peak concentration was generally similar in humans and monkeys.",

    "There is no strong evidence that human systemic clearance is more predictable from animal data than human oral clearance.",
    "Multiple linear regression of animal data generally predicts human clearance better than allometric methods.",

    "Human clearance can generally be predicted well from animal data with simple allometric scaling.",
    "Generating data in multiple non-human species does not always result in improved prediction.",
